title: Reliable access and availability of Ga-68 radiopharmaceuticals
summary: There when you need it: we asked five leaders across the nuclear medicine industry to share their specific experiences with one of the four key advantages of Gallium-68* (Ga-68) PET imaging: availability and reliable access on demand.
body_markdown:
*Gallium-68 (Ga-68) is a key radioisotope in nuclear medicine, largely employed in conjunction with specific ligands which target somatostatin receptors (SSTR) as a mechanism to accurately image neuroendocrine tumors (NET) as well as prostate specific membrane antigen (PSMA) in the imaging, diagnosis and staging of prostate cancer. Today, Ga-68 is the most widely used diagnostic isotope in ongoing theranostic clinical trials (source: clinicaltrials.gov analysis, data on file).


Safety statement: Gallium-68, when paired with a variety of targeting molecules (ligands), is a radioactive agent and should be handled by or under the control of qualified and licensed physicians with appropriate safety measures to help minimize radiation exposure. Any radiation-emitting product may increase the risk for cancer, especially in pediatric patients. Adhere to the respective dose recommendations for specific Ga-68 products and ensure safe handling to minimize the risk for excessive radiation exposure to either patients or healthcare workers.
